questions.text: Which first step is source-safe for a specialized health facility question?

options.text: Identify the actual use and the source table before choosing the occupancy path.
Apply a single room-area schedule to every clinic and hospital.
Treat all health facilities as assembly occupancies.
Use BP 344 dimensions even when the item asks only for PD 1096 occupancy.

questions.rationale: PD 1096 uses several checked entries for outpatient clinics, hospitals, nursing homes, medical centers, and multi-purpose clinics. The exact use controls.
questions.code_citation: DOH Manual on Technical Standards and Facilities for Primary Care

questions.text: Under RA 9514, which facility set is explicitly included in health care facilities?

options.text: Hospitals, nursing homes, and birth centers.
Barangay halls, gymnasiums, and convention halls.
Restaurants with less than 50 occupants.
Branch libraries and museums.

questions.rationale: RA 9514 lists hospitals, nursing homes, and birth centers as health care facilities.

questions.text: For a hospital or nursing home floor under RA 9514, what exit rule is source-safe?

options.text: At least two remote exits are required for each floor or fire section.
One exit is always enough if staff are present.
Elevators count as the required exits.
A lobby may replace all exits.

questions.rationale: RA 9514 requires at least two remote exits for each floor or fire section and states that elevators are supplementary, not required exits.

questions.text: What RA 9514 clear width applies to aisles, corridors, and ramps required for exit access in hospitals or nursing homes?

options.text: At least 2.44 m for hospital or nursing-home patient-use exit access.
At least 0.75 m for all patient corridors.
Exactly 1.00 m regardless of patient movement.
No clear width is specified for health care.

questions.rationale: RA 9514 states 2.44 m clear and unobstructed width for hospital or nursing-home exit access serving patient-use areas, with 1.83 m for adjunct areas not intended for inpatient housing, treatment, or use.
questions.code_citation: DOH Manual on Technical Standards and Facilities for Primary Care

questions.text: Which RA 9514 statement about health care smoke compartmentation is source-safe?

options.text: Storeys used by inpatients for sleeping or treatment are divided into at least two smoke compartments.
Smoke compartments are optional for all hospitals.
A single open floor is the default for inpatient sleeping areas.
Smoke partitions apply only to parking structures.

questions.rationale: RA 9514 requires smoke partitions to divide every storey used by inpatients for sleeping or treatment into at least two compartments.

questions.text: Which sprinkler rule is source-safe for hospitals and nursing homes under RA 9514?

options.text: Approved supervised sprinklers are required throughout, except for a one-storey building with bed capacity not exceeding five.
Sprinklers are never required in nursing homes.
Sprinklers are required only in lobbies.
Sprinklers are required only when a stage is present.

questions.rationale: RA 9514 requires approved supervised sprinklers throughout hospitals and nursing homes, with the stated one-storey, five-bed exception.

questions.text: If an exam item names an outpatient clinic rather than a hospital, what is the safest Batch 064 answer posture?

options.text: Use the stated facility use and table; do not automatically apply hospital-only rules.
Always classify it as a nursing home.
Ignore PD 1096 and answer from furniture clearances.
Assume it is an assembly hall.

questions.rationale: PD 1096 separately mentions outpatient clinics and hospitals in checked entries, so hospital-only rules should not be imported without the facts.
questions.code_citation: DOH Manual on Technical Standards and Facilities for Primary Care

questions.text: Which Fire Code general requirement supports specialized health facility egress review?

options.text: Exits must be of kind, number, location, and capacity appropriate to the occupancy and building conditions.
All exits may be locked if the owner prefers.
Egress can depend on one single safety feature.
Exit signs are optional in all occupied buildings.

questions.rationale: The Fire Code source family requires exits appropriate to the occupancy, occupant count, fire protection, height, and construction type.

questions.text: For emergency rooms, operating rooms, intensive care units, delivery rooms, and similar facilities, what does RA 9514 require as the basic location rule?

options.text: They shall be located on the level of exit discharge unless the stated alternate conditions are met.
They shall always be located below exit discharge.
They are exempt from exit discharge review.
They must be placed above the fifth floor.

questions.rationale: RA 9514 places those facilities on the level of exit discharge unless compliant ramp or horizontal-exit conditions are provided.
questions.code_citation: DOH Manual on Technical Standards and Facilities for Primary Care

questions.text: What does RA 9514 say about health care sleeping-room doors in the checked exit-access text?

options.text: A sleeping room without a ground-level outside door needs an exit-access door leading to a corridor that leads to an exit.
Sleeping rooms may rely only on windows for exit access.
Sleeping rooms never need corridor access.
Sleeping rooms must discharge through storage rooms.

questions.rationale: RA 9514 requires the health care sleeping room to have an exit-access door to a corridor leading to an exit, unless it opens at ground level.
questions.code_citation: DOH Manual on Technical Standards and Facilities for Primary Care
